answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable stake, then randomly assign it small tasks whose results are checked against independently staked peers. If an identity fabricates agreement or fails checks, its stake is slashed; honest work earns it back with a modest reward. A garden of agents can use a cipher to commit to answers before revealing them, limiting collusion through a whisper network. Sybils remain possible, but multiplying them means locking up more capital and risking repeated losses for little gain.
